name: Thuni (Nigerian)
description: Nigerian Thuni is a trick-taking game related to South African Thunee but played as a plain-trick game (no card points). The objective is winning tricks rather than counting card values, though the unusual ranking (J-9 high) remains.

overview.description: Nigerian Thuni is a trick-taking game related to South African Thunee but played as a plain-trick game (no card points). The objective is winning tricks rather than counting card values, though the unusual ranking (J-9 high) remains.

history.origins: Likely introduced by expatriates or travelers familiar with the South African or Indian versions.
timeline: 20th century: Played in Nigerian cities as plain-trick variant of Thunee.
history.evolution: Simplification of 304/Thunee to eliminate point counting.

setup.dealing: Deal 6 cards each (4 then 2) with 24-card deck, or 8 each with 32-card deck. Dealer offers cut to left.

rules.objective: Win the majority of tricks. No card points are counted; the game is played as plain-trick with the unusual ranking J-9-A-10-K-Q. Partners sit opposite and combine trick counts.
rules.gameplay: Dealer deals all cards (6 each with 24-card deck or 8 each with 32-card deck). Left of dealer leads to the first trick. Players must follow suit when able; otherwise may play any card. Highest card of the led suit wins the trick; trick winner leads next. Game ends when all tricks are played; side with more tricks wins.
